title: Rubio says Iran violated MOU within two weeks, leaves political outcome uncertain
description_short: Rubio said Iran violated an MOU within two weeks; he stated the U.S. shipping-defense objective but left Iran’s political outcome uncertain.
description_medium: At a July 19, 2026 press briefing, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran had violated a recent memorandum of understanding within two weeks. He separately described the U.S. mission as targeting Iranian assets used against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Asked what would happen if pro-diplomacy factions lost influence, he said he could not predict Iran’s internal outcome. The transcript supports the MOU timeline and the stated U.S. objective.
description_long: At Joint Base Andrews on July 19, 2026, Secretary of State Marco Rubio answered questions about Iran’s MOU, renewed attacks on shipping, and the war’s direction. Asked whether the memorandum was still alive, he said Iran was not complying and stated that Iran had made commitments in a recent MOU and violated it “within two weeks.” The transcript therefore supports the timing attributed to Rubio. In a separate exchange about renewed U.S. strikes, Rubio described the mission objective: target Iranian assets used to launch missiles and drones against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and defend ships using the international waterway. When asked what would happen if Iranian factions favoring diplomacy failed to gain influence, he said he could not tell how events would play out and that the outcome was up to Iran. That answer concerned Iran’s political trajectory; it does not show that Rubio lacked an articulated U.S. military objective. This corrected account retains his MOU statement while separating the exchanges and narrowing the “no endgame” characterization.
notes: Source-correction proposal only; no canonical or database record was changed.

title: Trump disclosure links nearly $800 million in reported 2025 income to WLF
description_short: Reuters said Trump’s 2025 disclosure tied nearly $800 million to World Liberty Financial, separate from $635 million in meme-coin income.
description_medium: Reuters’ June 30, 2026 review of Donald Trump’s 2025 financial disclosure reported more than $1.4 billion in income from family crypto ventures. The filing attributed almost $800 million to World Liberty Financial, including token and business-interest sales, and another $635 million to Trump meme-coin sales. These are reported income figures, not an audited net-profit calculation.
description_long: Reuters’ June 30, 2026 review of Donald Trump’s annual financial disclosure for 2025 reported more than $1.4 billion in income from crypto-related ventures. The report attributed almost $800 million to World Liberty Financial, the venture co-founded by Trump and his sons. Reuters said that figure included more than $520 million from token sales and more than $250 million from the sale of interests in the business. The report separately attributed $635 million to sales of Trump’s meme coin. The distinction matters: the record should not label the full $1.4 billion as World Liberty Financial income. Reuters also reported that the WLF income was split among family members. The disclosure and reporting describe income associated with the ventures, not an audited measure of net profit, cash personally retained by Trump, or company-wide revenue. These figures document the reported scale and composition of the crypto-related income; they do not by themselves establish that government policy caused or improperly benefited the ventures.
notes: Source-correction proposal only; no canonical or database record was changed.

title: Trump won Maison de l’Amitié auction and later sold property for $95 million
description_short: Trump won the 2004 bankruptcy auction for $41.35 million; Jeffrey Epstein was a competing bidder, and the property sold for $95 million in 2008.
description_medium: Donald Trump won the 2004 bankruptcy auction for Abe Gosman’s Palm Beach property, Maison de l’Amitié, with a $41.35 million bid. Jeffrey Epstein was a competing bidder, not a documented adviser. In 2008, Trump sold the property to a company controlled by Dmitry Rybolovlev’s family trust for $95 million, according to the cited reporting.
description_long: Donald Trump won the November 2004 bankruptcy auction for Abe Gosman’s Palm Beach oceanfront property, Maison de l’Amitié, with a $41.35 million bid, according to contemporaneous reporting. Jeffrey Epstein also bid in the auction, so the evidence describes him as a competitor rather than an adviser to Trump. A later Palm Beach Post report says Trump sold the property in 2008 for $95 million to a company controlled by a trust for Dmitry Rybolovlev’s family. The sale attracted public and congressional scrutiny because of the large price and the buyer’s ownership structure. The reported purchase and sale prices establish the transaction amounts, not Trump’s net profit: they do not account for carrying costs, investment, taxes, or other expenses. The cited reporting also does not establish money laundering or show that Epstein advised Trump. This account retains the documented auction and resale while removing the unsupported adviser and criminal-inference claims.
notes: Source-correction proposal only; no canonical or database record was changed.

title: OPM director says DOGE no longer existed as a centralized entity
description_short: In November 2025, Scott Kupor told Reuters DOGE no longer existed centrally, with about eight months left on its charter.
description_medium: Reuters reported that Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor said in November 2025 that DOGE “doesn’t exist” as a centralized entity, though its charter ran to July 2026. The article said OPM had taken over many of its functions. That statement describes DOGE’s organizational status; it does not establish that every related activity stopped or quantify spending and results.
description_long: Reuters reported on November 23, 2025, that Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor said the Department of Government Efficiency “doesn’t exist” as a centralized entity. The charter established for the initiative still had about eight months remaining, with an expiration in July 2026. Reuters also reported that OPM had taken over many DOGE functions and that former personnel had moved into other administration roles. The supported point is the reported end of DOGE as a central organization before its charter expired. It should not be expanded into a claim that every employee, function, or efficiency effort ended at once. The report also does not provide a final accounting of DOGE costs or independently measure whether it met its stated goals. Those spending and performance claims require separate evidence. This entry should be dated to the November status report rather than the original August 2025 framing and should distinguish the centralized entity from work that continued elsewhere in the government.
notes: Source-correction proposal only; no canonical or database record was changed.

title: Affinity Partners received $1.5 billion from Lunate and Qatar’s QIA in 2024
description_short: Reuters reported that Affinity received $1.5 billion in 2024 from Abu Dhabi-based Lunate and Qatar’s sovereign wealth fund.
description_medium: Reuters reported that Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners received $1.5 billion in additional capital in 2024 from existing investors Abu Dhabi-based Lunate and Qatar Investment Authority. Kushner said the capital had closed before Trump’s 2024 reelection; filings showed Affinity’s assets under management reached $4.8 billion at year-end. The report does not connect the capital to government policy.
description_long: Reuters reported that Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners received $1.5 billion in additional capital during 2024 from two existing investors: Abu Dhabi-based Lunate and Qatar’s sovereign wealth fund, the Qatar Investment Authority. The report said Kushner stated that the investment had closed before Donald Trump’s 2024 reelection and that filings showed Affinity’s assets under management reached $4.8 billion at the end of 2024. The corrected account identifies the investors and timing reported for this particular capital increase. It does not describe the $1.5 billion as a Saudi investment, nor does it establish that the capital was received while Kushner held a government position. Assets under management are a separate measure from the amount raised in this transaction. The report supports scrutiny of Affinity’s reported Gulf investor relationships, but it does not prove a quid pro quo or connection between the investment and U.S. policy. Those conclusions would require evidence beyond this financing report.

title: Trump Entertainment Resorts filed for Chapter 11 in February 2009
description_short: Trump Entertainment Resorts and two affiliated registrants reported voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on February 17, 2009.
description_medium: An SEC Form 8-K dated February 17, 2009, identifies Trump Entertainment Resorts, Inc. and two affiliated registrants and reports their voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in New Jersey bankruptcy court. The filing is primary evidence of the casino companies’ bankruptcy proceeding. It does not establish the separate claim that workers’ pensions or benefits were reduced.
description_long: Trump Entertainment Resorts, Inc., Trump Entertainment Resorts Holdings, L.P., and Trump Entertainment Resorts Funding, Inc. filed voluntary petitions for Chapter 11 relief in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey on February 17, 2009, according to the registrants’ SEC Form 8-K. The filing documents the bankruptcy event and identifies the companies involved; it placed these casino-related entities in a court-supervised reorganization process. It should not be read as a bankruptcy by Donald Trump personally or by every company carrying the Trump name. The filing describes financial restructuring involving debt and bondholder agreements, but the reviewed record does not substantiate the original claim that pension or benefit obligations were dramatically reduced for hundreds of workers. Nor does this one filing establish cumulative losses across several bankruptcies or whether Trump personally avoided all losses. Those impacts require separate documentation. The grounded account is the dated Chapter 11 filing by the named registrants.
notes: Source-correction proposal only; no canonical or database record was changed.

title: Trump says he sent Iran’s leader a nuclear-talks letter and warns of military action
description_short: Trump said he sent Iran’s leader a letter seeking nuclear talks and warned that military action would be terrible if negotiations failed.
description_medium: On March 7, 2025, Trump said he had sent a letter to Iran’s Supreme Leader seeking a new nuclear agreement and said he preferred a deal. He also warned that military action would be a “terrible thing” and publicly said something would happen soon. The reports support a warning, not the original February deadline or a detailed ultimatum.
description_long: On March 7, 2025, Trump said he had sent a letter to Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei seeking negotiations over Iran’s nuclear program; he said it was sent the day before. The Associated Press reported that he preferred a peace deal but warned that military action would be “a terrible thing” if the United States had to resort to it. Trump also told reporters that something would happen with Iran “very soon.” Reuters likewise reported the letter and his stated preference for a negotiated deal as his administration restored a maximum-pressure campaign. These reports support a diplomatic overture paired with an explicit but nonspecific military warning. They do not establish the entry’s claimed February 10 deadline, a compressed compliance schedule, or a specific set of terms Iran had to accept. The corrected account dates the public reporting to March and describes the warning in the terms attributed to Trump rather than converting it into a formal strike ultimatum with a fixed deadline.
notes: Source-correction proposal only; no canonical or database record was changed.
